Vijayapura, In M.V.C No.231/2017.
 These Appeals, Coming On For Further Hearing,
This Day, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

Challenging common judgment and separate awards dated 07.08.2019 passed by III Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-XII, Vijaypur (for short 'tribunal') in MVC nos.224/2017 to 227/2017 and 231/2017, these appeals are filed.

The Divisional Controller vs Kamalabai And Ors on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195777776/
8 2.

entities.text: Divisional Controller vs Kamalabai And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While MFA.nos.202223/2019, 202219/2019, 202220/2019, 202221/2019 and 202222/2019 are by KSRTC, challenging award of tribunal about negligence as - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7493 well as on quantum, MFA.nos.200236/2020 and 200237/2020 are by claimants for enhancement of compensation.

3. Shri Sharanabasappa M. Patil, learned counsel for appellant submitted that as per claimants, on 06.01.2017, when they were travelling in a passenger Auto-rickshaw bearing registration no.KA-28/A-4685 from Torvi to Vijaypur, driver of bus belonging to KSRTC bearing registration no.KA-28/F-2044, drove it in rash and negligent manner and dashed against Auto-rickshaw causing accident.
In said accident, claimants sustained grievous injuries.
Despite taking treatment, they did not recover fully.
Claiming compensation, they filed claim petitions under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act against KSRTC as well as owner and insurer of Auto-rickshaw.
4. Despite service of notice, owner of Auto- rickshaw did not appear and contest and he was placed - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7493 ex parte.
Respondent-KSRTC opposed claim petitions on ground that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Auto-rickshaw by its driver.
It was also submitted that compensation claimed was excessive.
5. Based on pleadings, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.
Seven witnesses were examined by claimants as PWs.1 to 7 and Exs.P1 to P31 were marked.

Respondents examined driver as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R1.
6.
On consideration, tribunal held that, accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of bus by its driver and claimants were entitled for compensation as assessed from KSRTC.

Aggrieved,
above appeals are filed.
7.
Insofar as negligence, learned counsel for KSRTC submitted that in respect of accident, even KSRTC driver had sought to give complaint.
As it was not accepted at police station, it was tendered to - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7493 Superintendent of Police.
Merely on ground that there was some delay in filing complaint, tribunal refused to take it into account.
As mere delay cannot be sole reason for over looking complaint, it had to be considered.
Same would dilute reliance placed by claimants on police investigation records.

It was submitted that KSRTC had examined its driver as RW.1 who had stated that at accident spot, driver of bus had stopped for alighting passengers and had just begun moving bus, when Auto-rickshaw came and dashed against bus.

It was further contended that at The Divisional Controller vs Kamalabai And Ors on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195777776/
9 time of accident, Auto-rickshaw was carrying excessive passengers far more than permit limit and due to excessive load, driver was unable to control it and caused accident.

entities.text: Divisional Controller vs Kamalabai And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, driver of Auto-rickshaw was negligent in causing accident.
8. Alternatively, it was submitted that since accident was a head-on-collision, both drivers were - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7493 required to be held responsible and negligence apportioned accordingly.
9. Insofar as quantum, it was submitted that Kashibai-claimant in MVC no.224/2017 had sustained simple injuries.
Despite same, tribunal awarded `25,000/-, which was excessive.
Likewise, even Kamalabai - claimant in MVC no.225/2017 and Sunanda-claimant in MVC no.227/2017 had also sustained simple injuries and award of `15,000/- each was excessive.
10. It was further submitted that Kamalabai Natikar - claimant in MVC No.226/2017 had sustained fracture of mandible, which would not lead to loss of earning capacity.
However, tribunal assessed functional disability at 20% and awarded excessive compensation.
11. Further, though Smt.Rashida Akbar Nadaf - claimant in MVC no.231/2017 had sustained fractures, X-ray report noted that fractures were united.

Therefore,
- 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7493 considering functional disability at 10% was unjustified.

On above grounds,
sought for reduction.
12. On other hand, Shri Sanganagouda V. Biradar, learned counsel submitted that appeals by claimants were for enhancement of compensation.
Insofar as appeals by KSRTC, it was submitted that though driver had given complaint, same was an after thought.
It was submitted that driver was arrested on very date of accident and thereafter released on bail.
As admitted by him in cross- examination, complaint was filed as per advise of KSRT Law Officer.
In any case, driver had failed to challenge charge sheet filed against him.
Under such circumstances, reliance placed by tribunal on prosecution records was justified.
13. For enhancement, it was submitted that there were several injuries sustained by claimants, for which they took inpatient treatment.
Despite same, instead of - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7493 assessing compensation separately under various heads, award of global compensation was unjustified.
It was submitted that though accident occurred in year 2017 and The Divisional Controller vs Kamalabai And Ors on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195777776/

entities.text: Divisional Controller vs Kamalabai And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10 notional income for said period was `10,250/-, tribunal had assessed compensation by taking `7,000/- per month as income.
Hence compensation awarded did not call for interference.
14. Even in MVC nos.226/2017 and 231/2017, assessment of compensation was not commensurate to injuries/disability sustained and called for enhancement.

15. Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and award.
16.

From above submission, since KSRTC is challenging award about negligence and also on quantum, while claimants seeking enhancement of compensation, points that would arise for consideration are:
- 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7493 "(i) Whether finding of tribunal on negligence against KSRTC driver calls for interference?
(ii) Whether compensation assessed by tribunal calls for modification?"
Point no.(i) - Negligence 17.

To establish actionable negligence against driver of KSRTC and owner and insurer of Auto-rickshaw, claimants relied mainly on police investigation records, such as FIR, Complaint,
Spot-panchanama, Motor Vehicle Inspector's report and Charge-Sheet marked as Exs.P1 to P5 and P13 respectively.
18. Perusal of Ex.P1 would indicate that same is registered on basis of complaint given by one of inmates of Auto-rickshaw.
It would impute entire negligence against KSRTC driver in causing accident.
Ex.P13- chargesheet is also filed against only KSRTC bus driver.

RW.1, driver of bus stepped into witness box and stated - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7493 that when he approached police, his complaint was not registered and therefore, complaint marked as Ex.R1 was submitted to Superintendent of Police on 09.01.2017.

However, merely on ground that driver had given complaint that too after lapse of three days,
contributory negligence cannot be presumed against driver of Auto rickshaw.

19. It is also seen that in Ex.R1, RW.1- driver had stated that at time of accident, vehicle was moving slowly and cautiously after alighting passengers, when Auto- rickshaw came from opposite direction after over-taking a lorry and dashed against bus.
Whereas in deposition, he states that at time of accident, he had stopped bus for alighting passengers, when Auto-rickshaw came and dashed against bus.
Said material contradiction is without explanation.

The Divisional Controller vs Kamalabai And Ors on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195777776/
11 - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7493 20.

entities.text: Divisional Controller vs Kamalabai And Ors on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
While claimants relied upon police investigation records, which is an independent agency;
KSRTC seeks to rely on self-serving statement of driver.
Ex. P13
- Charge sheet is filed against driver of bus alone.
Therefore, finding of tribunal on negligence would not call for interference.
Point no.1 is thus, answered in negative.
Point no.(ii) - Quantum of compensation 21.

In MFA.202223/2019, it is seen that claimant Kashibai, aged 40 years and stated to be earning `15,000/- per month from agriculture, sustained 'V' shaped injury over right fronto parietal region and abrasion over right eyebrow.
22. As per wound certificate, injuries are simple in nature.
However, tribunal observed that claimant produced medical bills for `17,130/-.

Considering same, award of `25,000/- globally by tribunal in facts and circumstances of this case, cannot be stated to be grossly - 19 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7493 excessive or contrary to evidence on record.
Hence, compensation awarded is confirmed.

In MFA no.202219/2019 connected with MFA no.200237/2020 :
23.
Claimant - Rashida is aged 45 years stated to be earning `15,000/- per month from agriculture.
She sustained fracture of right femur, right fibula, fracture of mandible on right hand.
Said injuries were assessed by PW.6-Doctor to have caused 30% physical disability.
However, tribunal has considered loss of earning capacity by 10%.

For said injuries, tribunal has awarded compensation under following heads :-
1. Pain and suffering 15,000/-
2. Medical expenses 1,62,000/-
3. Loss of income due to functional physical 1,17,600/- disability 4.

Food and nourishment 2,000/-
5.

Attendant charges 2,000/-
6.
Conveyance charges 2,000/-

7. Loss of amenities and future 5,000/-

12 unhappiness

entities.text: Divisional Controller vs Kamalabai And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even claimant is in appeal for enhancement.
Though claimant stated that she was earning `15,000/- per month, same is not substantiated with evidence.

In absence of specific evidence,
tribunal would be justified notionally.
Notional income for year 2017 is `10,250/- same has to be taken.
25. Though PW.6 has assessed disability at 30%, in cross-examination it is elicited that fractures are united.

5. Based on pleadings, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.

Respondents examined driver as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R1.
6.
On consideration, tribunal held that, accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of bus by its driver and claimants were entitled for compensation as assessed from KSRTC.
However, tribunal assessed functional disability at 20% and awarded excessive compensation.
Hence compensation awarded did not call for interference.
Thus, compensation would be `2,06,640/- (`10,250 X 12% X 12 X 14).
31.

32. Since claimant has sustained fracture and disability, award of `5,000/- towards 'loss of amenities' would be inadequate.
